messages:
sam walker: FYI nightly eval run #02 had 3 intermittent failures, harness hit the 10m test timeout repeatedly. logs show worker stuck with no stdout for minutes. :frowning:

maya liu: which tests are failing? can you paste the log snippet or run link?

sam walker: failing suites: prompt-regression/test-parse, generation/length-sanity, rerank/stability. snippet:

```
Thread 7 - worker-42 - waiting in epoll_wait
stack: poll -> epoll_wait -> futex_wait -> pthread_cond_wait
last_output: "prompt: compute logits..."
cpu% (user+sys): 0.2, cpu_steal: 28.7
```

sam walker: not sure if it's a harness bug or infra noise, but the worker never recovers, just sits there until timeout.

alex ramos: smells like CPU steal / ephemeral scheduling starvation on CI VM. we had noisy neighbor backups scheduled last night on those hosts. can you check host metrics (iowait/steal)?

ci-bot: run: https://ci.redwood.ai/runs/45321 - metrics attached (cpu_steal spike ~30% between 00:08:00-00:12:00) :chart_with_upwards_trend:

jen carr: we changed the sandboxing cpuset controller last week to isolate workers. maybe the cgroup assignment is flaky and some workers end up with 0 cpus. worth checking systemd/cgroup logs.

maya liu: i repro locally on an m4-small by running 50 parallel workers, hangs show up after ~8m. command i used:

```
./tools/run_eval_harness --parallel 50 --suite "prompt-regression" --timeout 600
```

maya liu: when i throttle CPU with `cpulimit` i can trigger the same epoll_wait hang. seems like the harness doesn't detect lack of progress, no heartbeat.

sam walker: quick mitigation: PR submitted to reduce default parallelism from 32 -> 8 and add a per-worker watchdog that kills and respawns if no stdout for 2m. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/eval-harness/pull/789 :hammer_and_wrench:

alex ramos: also adding a cheap liveness probe in the worker loop (increment a counter to shared shm every 10s) so the master can evict stuck workers sooner. not ideal but will cut flakes while infra root cause is investigated.

infra-bot: infra note: we observed kernel upgrade + cpuset behavior changes rolled 2 days ago to the autoscaler images. scheduling policy reverted on a subset of hosts. ticket: INF-2219.

jen carr: plan: 1) land reduced-parallelism to staging, 2) add worker watchdog + liveness to harness, 3) add CI micro-check that fails the run if cpu_steal > 20% during execution, 4) infra to roll back cpuset kernel patch on subset for comparison.

sam walker: after reducing parallelism the flake rate dropped from ~12->1 in the last 3 runs. will run a bisect next to see if the kernel change correlates. i'll follow up with a short postmortem once we confirm root cause. :eyes:

maya liu: thanks all. i'll take the reproduce notes and add to the eval-harness troubleshooting doc.

alex ramos: one more ask - can we surface `cpu_steal` in the test failure UI so teams can triage faster? filing frontend ticket now.

sam walker: good call. tagging folks for visibility: @jen carr @alex ramos @maya liu @infra-bot
